To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the use of a histogram based on flows volume leads to better detection performance than the histogram based on flows destination address; and (ii) the use of three dimensional sketches leads to better detection results than the use of the original traffic traces.

the use of sketches is a viable alternative to the use of counters and that the entropy computed over the histogram based on the flows volume is more informative than the one computed over the histogram built on the flows destination.

the entropy of the number of flows is a more robust metric than the entropy of the byte count and that the use of the flows destination address as a basis for the construction of the histogram is more effective than the use of their volume.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) what is the impact of histogram construction techniques on the detection accuracy? and (ii) what is the role of traffic aggregation techniques in the anomaly detection process?

the following issues: (1) the use of random data structures to efficiently summarize network traffic; (2) the application of information theory to anomaly detection; and (3) the impact of different histogram construction techniques.
the following questions: (i) is it possible to build an anomaly detector based on entropy?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(i) the entropy computed by considering the flows destination address provides a more robust detection capability than that obtained by considering the flows volume and (ii) the entropy computed on a histogram constructed by means of the sketching technique is more robust than that computed on a histogram obtained by using a classical data structure (namely the histogram) and the same number of bins.

, when using entropy as anomaly detection metric, a more accurate histogram construction is obtained by using a finer grained aggregation of the flows, namely the volume, rather than the destination address.

the entropy computed over the volume based histogram provides a good measure of anomaly detection, but it is not robust to the traffic variability, whereas the entropy computed over a flow based histogram is more stable, but not able to detect the attacks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the entropy of the number of bytes is a good indicator of the traffic normalcy, while the entropy of the flow number is not.
the entropy of the volume histogram is more sensitive to the presence of anomalies, but the one of the address histogram is more robust to the presence of false alarms.

, when the histogram is constructed by using the destination address, the system is more robust with respect to the presence of background traffic, but it is less effective in detecting the attacks, whereas, the opposite is true when the histogram is built by using the flow volume.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the entropy of the volume histogram is more sensitive to anomalies than that of the address histogram.
the choice of the histogram construction technique has a significant impact on the performance of the anomaly detector.
, by exploiting a simple and efficient data structure, the proposed system can effectively identify the presence of attacks, even when they are very short.
